newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila steel firm sees 2.5 bln peso loss in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Manila steel firm sees 2.5 bln peso loss in 1996.

text.p: Philippines' National Steel Corp (NSC) suffered a 2.56 billion peso net loss last year, down from a 587.41 million profit a year earlier, it told the Securities and Exchange Commission on Wednesday.
The unlisted firm's revenues were 12.71 billion pesos, slightly higher than 12.59 billion in 1995.
An NSC official attributed the small revenue growth to low tariff rates imposed on steel imports, undercutting NSC prices.
Expenses also grew to 15.73 billion pesos against 11.88 billion in 1995.

National Steel, the country's biggest producer of semi-finished steel products, is majority owned by Hottic Investments Ltd of Hong Kong. The Philippine government owns 12.5 percent. ($1 = 26.3 pesos)
